reviews.body: > ✅ No new issues found. **Reviewed changes** Reviewed the change that moves the MCP toolset wrapper out of `_toolset.py`, so `restate.ext.pydantic` can be imported without the `pydantic-ai-slim[mcp]` extra. - **MCP wrapper moved to `_mcp_toolset.py`**: `RestateMCPToolset`, `RestateMCPGetToolsContextRunResult`, `RestateMCPToolRunResult` and their serdes are moved over unchanged, and the top-level `from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPToolset` goes with them. - **Lazy import updated**: the guarded `try/except ImportError` in `RestateAgent.__init__`'s `set_context` now imports from `._mcp_toolset`. `pydantic_ai/mcp.py` re-raises a missing `mcp`/`fastmcp` as `ImportError`, so the guard catches it. - **Regression test**: `tests/pydantic_ai_without_mcp.py` sets `sys.modules['pydantic_ai.mcp'] = None` in a subprocess and imports the extension. On the base commit this fails, because `_toolset.py` imports `pydantic_ai.mcp` at module level. What I checked: - `main` (`0d06f2c`) still has the module-level import, so the fix is still needed. - Nothing else on `main` imports `RestateMCPToolset` or the MCP serdes from `_toolset`. - GitHub reports the PR as mergeable against current `main`. - On the PR head, the new test passes, and `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` on `python/restate/ext/pydantic/` all pass.   ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/restatedev/sdk-python/actions/runs/42255849334/job/128022711333) ｜ Using `claude-opus-5-5` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)
